stem.text: Water flows into a tank at the rate \( R(t) = 3 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2} \right)} + 11 \) gallons per hour, where t is measured in hours for \( 0 \le t \le 5 \). The tank holds 20 gallons of water at time \( t = 0 \). During the same time, water flows out through a drain at the rate \( D(t) = t + \frac{11}{2} \) gallons per hour. Using a calculator, find the total number of gallons that arrive during the time interval \( 0 \le t \le 4 \). Show the setup, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The amount that arrives is the integral of the inflow rate over the interval, \( \int_{0}^{4} \left(3 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2} \right)} + 11\right)\,dt \), and nothing is added for the starting amount or taken away.
With the calculator in radian mode, the integral is about 46.723 gallons.

options.derivation: the integral evaluated with the calculator in degree mode
the rate evaluated at the endpoints and subtracted, R(b) - R(a), in place of its integral
the amount present at the end reported, the starting amount added to the integral of the inflow
